column1: [CMP-23] Implement document version history
column30:
*Requirement type:* Functional
*Related requirements:* FR-005, BR-003, NFR-013
*MoSCoW:* Must
*Estimated effort:* 5 SP / 10 h
*Blocked by:* CMP-21, CMP-22

h3. Goal
Keep a complete, immutable history of document versions, where a new version becomes current only after it is processed successfully.

h3. Tech stack
* Laravel {{POST /api/documents/\{id\}/versions}} ({{StoreDocumentVersionRequest}}), {{DocumentVersionService::makeCurrent()}}.
* React tab "Versions" in {{/documents/\{id\}}}.

h3. Implementation details
* New version: same validations as CMP-20/CMP-21; stored with is_current = false and status 'queued'.
* When processing succeeds, one transaction sets the previous version is_current = false, the new one is_current = true, calls FastAPI set-current (CMP-29) and writes audit document_version.set_current.
* If processing fails, the previous version stays current and the uploader sees the message below.
* Versions tab table columns: Version, Uploaded by, Upload date, Status, Expiration date, Current (badge "Current"), Download (button).
* No DELETE route exists for documents or versions; PUT/PATCH on a version returns 403.
* Button "Upload new version" visible only to roles that can upload.

h3. Exact messages
||Case||HTTP||Exact text shown||
|New version fails processing|-|Version <new label> could not be processed. Version <current label> remains the current version.|
|Attempt to modify or delete a version|403 / 405|Document versions cannot be modified or deleted.|

h3. Acceptance criteria
# Uploading version 2.0 keeps 1.0 as current while 2.0 is queued/processing; after success 2.0 shows the "Current" badge.
# Version 1.0 remains listed and downloadable from the Versions tab.
# A version 3.0 that fails processing leaves 2.0 as current and shows the exact message.
# PATCH/DELETE requests on a version return the exact message; audit records exist for created and set_current versions.

h3. Definition of done
* Code merged into {{develop}} through a Pull Request titled "CMP-23: Implement document version history" with at least 1 approval.

column1: [CMP-38] Implement security audit logging and audit-record protection
column30:
*Requirement type:* Non-functional
*Related requirements:* NFR-014, NFR-013, BR-008
*MoSCoW:* Must
*Estimated effort:* 5 SP / 8 h
*Blocked by:* CMP-37, CMP-08

h3. Goal
Record security events with enough detail to investigate incidents, and make audit records impossible to change or delete.

h3. Tech stack
* Laravel listeners on auth events ({{Login}}, {{Failed}}, {{Logout}}, {{Lockout}}) + {{AuditLogger}} with category 'security'.
* PostgreSQL trigger and privileges on {{audit_logs}}.
* React read-only viewer {{/admin/audit-log}}.

h3. Implementation details
* Events: auth.login_succeeded, auth.login_failed (metadata: attempted email), auth.logout, auth.account_locked, access.denied, user.created, user.role_changed, user.deactivated, user.activated, document.download_denied, audit.modification_denied.
* Every record: user_id (null for failed logins with unknown email), action, resource, IP address (real client IP via TrustProxies), user agent, timestamp.
* Protection layer 1 (app): AuditLog model throws {{AuditLogImmutableException}} on updating/deleting; no update/delete routes.
* Protection layer 2 (database): trigger {{prevent_audit_log_changes}} BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE that raises an exception; and {{REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE ON audit_logs FROM compliance_app}}.
* Viewer {{/admin/audit-log}}: filters date range, user, category, action; 50 rows per page; columns Date/time, User, Action, Resource, IP. Read-only. Access per ADR-005 (Administrator; Compliance Staff only if confirmed).

h3. Exact messages
||Case||HTTP||Exact text shown||
|Attempt to modify/delete an audit record via API|403|Audit records cannot be modified or deleted.|
|Direct UPDATE/DELETE in database|-|PostgreSQL error: "audit_logs records are immutable".|

h3. Acceptance criteria
# Pest tests assert a record with user, action, resource, IP and timestamp for: successful login, failed login, access denial and role change.
# {{UPDATE audit_logs SET action='x' WHERE id=1}} as the app DB user fails; screenshot attached.
# A PUT/DELETE to {{/api/audit-logs/1}} returns 403 with the exact message and creates audit.modification_denied.

column1: [CMP-40] Configure automated daily database backups with monitoring
column30:
*Requirement type:* Non-functional
*Related requirements:* NFR-015
*MoSCoW:* Must
*Estimated effort:* 3 SP / 6 h
*Blocked by:* CMP-05, CMP-06

h3. Goal
Back up the database every day automatically and detect immediately when a backup fails.

h3. Tech stack
* Docker container {{db-backup}} (postgres:16 image + cron + gnupg + rclone).
* Off-server storage: S3-compatible bucket (e.g., Backblaze B2 or AWS S3) per ADR-030.
* Monitoring: Healthchecks.io (free plan) or an Uptime Kuma push monitor, email alerts to the team.

h3. Implementation details
* Script {{infra/backup/backup.sh}} runs daily at 02:30 America/Mexico_City: {{pg_dump -Fc}} -> {{gpg --symmetric --cipher-algo AES256}} (if ADR-033 says encrypt) -> upload with rclone to {{backups/db/compliance_YYYYMMDD_HHMM.dump.gpg}}.
* Also archives the {{documents_storage}} volume (already encrypted files) weekly.
* Each run appends a line to {{/var/log/backup.log}}: start time, end time, file name, size in bytes, result OK/FAILED.
* On success the script calls the monitoring ping URL; on any error ({{set -euo pipefail}} + trap) it calls the /fail URL.
* Alert email subject: "\[Compliance Platform\] Daily backup FAILED" with the error output; also sent if no ping arrives within 26 hours.
* Procedure documented in {{docs/operations/backups.md}}.

h3. Acceptance criteria
# The bucket shows one backup file per day for at least 3 consecutive days, each with date and time in the name; backup.log shows OK for each.
# Forcing a failure (wrong DB password) triggers the alert email with the exact subject within 15 minutes; screenshot attached.
# The backup file cannot be opened without the GPG passphrase (if encryption is required).

column1: [CMP-18] Implement missing-document detection
column30:
*Requirement type:* Functional
*Related requirements:* FR-014
*MoSCoW:* Must
*Estimated effort:* 5 SP / 8 h
*Blocked by:* CMP-15, CMP-20, CMP-04

h3. Goal
Show clearly which required documents of each compliance requirement are missing.

h3. Tech stack
* Laravel service {{RequiredDocumentStatusService}} implementing the ADR-022 rule (CMP-04).
* React components in {{/requirements/\{id\}}} and the requirements list.

h3. Implementation details
* Rule (from ADR-022): satisfied when a linked document exists AND category matches AND its current version is 'processed' AND expiration is empty or after today.
* Link UI: each required document row has "Link document" (search among documents of the same category) and "Unlink".
* Row display: green badge "Provided" with the document name as link, or red badge "Missing Document". When the linked document is expired, red badge "Missing Document" with tooltip "The linked document expired on <DD/MM/YYYY>.". When the linked version is still processing: gray badge "Processing".
* Requirements list shows a counter: "<n> missing documents" in red, or "All documents provided" in green.
* Status is recalculated on document processed, version changed, link/unlink, and daily at 00:05 for expirations.
* Audit: requirement.document_linked / requirement.document_unlinked.

||Case||HTTP||Exact text shown||
|Linking a document with a different category|422|This document's category (<doc category>) does not match the required category (<required category>).|
|Linking a document of another organization or not accessible|403|You do not have permission to link this document.|

h3. Acceptance criteria
# A requirement with a required document and no linked document shows "Missing Document".
# Linking a processed document of the right category changes it to "Provided" without a page reload.

column1: [CMP-30] Implement permission-aware retrieval
column30:
*Requirement type:* Functional
*Related requirements:* FR-011, AIR-002, AIR-006, BR-002
*MoSCoW:* Must
*Estimated effort:* 8 SP / 14 h
*Blocked by:* CMP-29, CMP-10

h3. Goal
Retrieve only fragments from documents the user is allowed to see, before any answer is generated.

h3. Tech stack
* Laravel {{DocumentPolicy}} + query scope {{Document::visibleTo($user)}} to compute allowed IDs.
* FastAPI retrieval module with pgvector SQL query.
* Structured JSON logs (Python logging + python-json-logger).

h3. Implementation details
* Laravel computes {{allowed_document_ids}} for the user (organization + role + access_level) and sends them in /v1/ask. FastAPI never receives a user-chosen list from React.
* SQL pre-filter (filter inside the query, not after): {{WHERE organization_id = :org AND document_id = ANY(:allowed) AND is_current ORDER BY embedding <=> :query_embedding LIMIT :top_k}}.
* Similarity = 1 - cosine distance; fragments below the ADR-013 threshold are discarded.
* If allowed_document_ids is empty or no fragment passes the threshold, return the insufficient-information response (CMP-31) without calling the LLM.
* Logs per request_id: event "retrieval_started", "retrieval_finished" (fragments_considered, fragments_kept, top_score), then "generation_started"; timestamps prove order.

h3. Acceptance criteria
# Logs of 10 test questions show retrieval_finished before generation_started for every request.
# Test with 2 users: a 'compliance_only' document is cited for Compliance Staff; for General Employee the same question returns the insufficient-information response and no chunk of that document appears in the logs.
# pytest: fragments with similarity below the threshold are never passed to the LLM.

h3. Definition of done
* Code merged into {{develop}} through a Pull Request titled "CMP-30: Implement permission-aware retrieval" with at least 1 approval.
* Automated tests for this task added and passing in GitHub Actions.

column1: [CMP-11] Implement account lockout after 5 failed logins
column30:
*Requirement type:* Non-functional
*Related requirements:* NFR-006
*MoSCoW:* Should
*Estimated effort:* 2 SP / 4 h
*Blocked by:* CMP-08

h3. Goal
Block brute-force password guessing by locking an account for 15 minutes after 5 consecutive failed sign-ins.

h3. Tech stack
* Laravel: columns users.failed_login_attempts and users.locked_until (CMP-06), logic inside {{AuthController@login}}.
* React message on the login page.

h3. Implementation details
* Each failed attempt for an existing email increments failed_login_attempts; a successful login resets it to 0.
* On the 5th consecutive failure: locked_until = now + 15 minutes, security audit auth.account_locked.
* While locked, any attempt (even with the right password) is rejected with HTTP 423 and does not increase the counter.
* After locked_until passes, the next correct sign-in succeeds and resets the counter.
* Attempts with unknown emails do not reveal whether the email exists (same generic message as CMP-08 until a lock applies).
* Times shown in America/Mexico_City, 24-hour format.

h3. Exact messages
||Case||HTTP||Exact text shown||
|5th consecutive failed attempt|423|Your account has been locked for 15 minutes due to too many failed sign-in attempts. Try again at <HH:mm>.|
|Any attempt during the lock|423|Your account is locked. Try again in <n> minutes.|

h3. Acceptance criteria
# After 5 wrong passwords the 5th response shows the exact lock message with the correct time.
# During the lock the correct password is rejected with "Your account is locked. Try again in <n> minutes.".
# Pest test with {{Carbon::setTestNow(+16 minutes)}} confirms login works and failed_login_attempts = 0.
# An auth.account_locked audit record exists.

column1: [CMP-31] Implement grounded answer generation and insufficient-information response
column30:
*Requirement type:* Non-functional
*Related requirements:* NFR-018, AIR-003, AIR-005, AIR-007, BR-005, BR-006, BR-007
*MoSCoW:* Must
*Estimated effort:* 5 SP / 10 h
*Blocked by:* CMP-30

h3. Goal
Generate answers only from retrieved fragments, admit when there is not enough information, and always show the not-legal-advice disclaimer.

h3. Tech stack
* FastAPI service, Python 3.12, LLM from ADR-010 through ProviderClient (CMP-28).
* Versioned prompt file {{ai-service/app/prompts/answer_v1.txt}}.

h3. Implementation details
* System prompt rules: answer only with the numbered context fragments; cite each fact with \[n\]; if the fragments do not contain the answer reply exactly with the insufficient-information text; answer in the language of the question; do not give legal advice; do not invent document names.
* Parameters: temperature 0.1, max output 800 tokens, timeout 10 s.
* Post-check: if the answer contains no valid \[n\] reference to a provided fragment, replace it with the insufficient-information response (status "insufficient_information").
* Insufficient-information text (exact, shown to the user): "I could not find enough information in your organization's documents to answer this question."
* Disclaimer text (exact, always returned in {{disclaimer}} and shown under every answer): "This answer is generated from your organization's documents and is not legal advice. Verify important decisions with a qualified legal professional."
* If the question is in Spanish, both texts are returned in Spanish: "No encontré suficiente información en los documentos de tu organización para responder esta pregunta." and "Esta respuesta se genera a partir de los documentos de tu organización y no constituye asesoría legal. Verifica las decisiones importantes con un profesional legal calificado."

h3. Exact messages
||Case||HTTP||Exact text shown||
|No fragment passes the threshold|200|I could not find enough information in your organization's documents to answer this question.|
|LLM timeout (10 s)|504|The assistant took too long to respond. Please try again.|

h3. Acceptance criteria
# pytest with mocked LLM: the prompt sent contains only retrieved fragments.
# With no fragment over the threshold the exact insufficient-information text is returned and the LLM is not called.
# Every answer (answered or insufficient) includes the exact disclaimer and the UI shows it.
# All evaluation questions without supporting documents (CMP-36) return the insufficient-information response.

column1: [CMP-27] Implement search and filtering for documents and requirements
column30:
*Requirement type:* Functional
*Related requirements:* FR-009, BR-002
*MoSCoW:* Should
*Estimated effort:* 5 SP / 10 h
*Blocked by:* CMP-21, CMP-15

h3. Goal
Let users find documents and requirements quickly with filters, seeing only what they are allowed to access.

h3. Tech stack
* React pages {{/documents}} and {{/requirements}} with a filter bar; filters kept in URL query parameters.
* Laravel query scopes; PostgreSQL {{unaccent}} + ILIKE for accent- and case-insensitive name search.

h3. Implementation details
* Documents filters: Name (text), Category (multi-select), Processing status, Upload date from/to, Expiration date from/to. API {{GET /api/documents?name=&category\[\]=&status=&uploaded_from=&uploaded_to=&expires_from=&expires_to=&page=}}.
* Requirements filters: Name, Status (multi-select), Regulation (text), Deadline from/to. API {{GET /api/compliance-requirements?...}}.
* All filters combine with AND; the authorization scope (CMP-10) is applied before filters.
* Text inputs search after 300 ms without typing (debounce); pagination 20 per page; button "Clear filters".
* Results count text: "<n> results".

h3. Exact messages
||Case||HTTP||Exact text shown||
|No results|-|No results found. Try changing or clearing the filters.|
|'From' date after 'to' date|422|The 'from' date must be before or equal to the 'to' date.|
|Invalid date in a filter|422|Enter a valid date.|

h3. Acceptance criteria
# Searching "politica" finds "Política de Seguridad" (accent-insensitive).
# Combining category + expiration range returns only documents that meet both (Pest).
# A General Employee never receives 'compliance_only' documents in results.

* Report shows each metric, its threshold, PASS/FAIL, and a list of failed questions with the reason.

h3. Acceptance criteria

# Report {{eval/reports/<date>/report.md}} and {{results.csv}} committed with all metrics and PASS/FAIL against ADR-013.
# 100% of document-based answers include the source document name.

* Maintenance windows from ADR-032 (proposal Sunday 02:00-04:00 America/Mexico_City) configured as maintenance so they do not count as downtime.

* Monthly report {{docs/operations/availability-<YYYY-MM>.md}}: availability %, number of incidents, total downtime minutes, target 99%. Because the project ends in December, the report covers the period from deployment to the report date.

h3. Acceptance criteria

# A check during the maintenance window is not counted as downtime (screenshot).

* Tags: {{type:standard}} for normal requests, {{type:ai}} for /api/assistant/questions.
* Thresholds: {{http_req_duration\{type:standard\}: p(95)<2000}} and {{http_req_duration\{type:ai\}: p(90)<10000}}; error rate < 1%.
* Report {{docs/qa/performance-report.md}}: environment specs, load profile, results table, % standard requests under 2 s (target 95%), % AI answers under 10 s (target 90%), bottlenecks found and actions.

h3. Acceptance criteria
# Load test executed with at least 100 concurrent users following ADR-031; k6 summary and HTML report attached.
# Report states both percentages and PASS/FAIL; any FAIL has a linked Bug.
